claims.head: A tough night ahead for Aho

claims.head: Lankinen is due against the Hurricanes
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Lankinen has been shaky against the Hurricanes, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.

claims.gist: Don’t read much into Lankinen’s record against the Hurricanes.

notes.text: Seth Jarvis is out and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. William Carrier has taken his spot beside Sebastian Aho and Andrei Svechnikov.
Taylor Hall is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game.
Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 2 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.
Alexander Nikishin has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Mike Reilly has taken his spot beside Shayne Gostisbehere.
Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 46% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 64 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (17 of 20 changes).

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 45%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Marco Rossi is out (illness) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Max Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, up from 4% last season.

VAN.head: A steep climb for the Canucks
VAN.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks’ best hope is getting good looks, plus a big night in goal.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes should be in control
CAR.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks’ best way in is getting good looks.

story.head: The Hurricanes are rolling
paras: The Hurricanes won the first meeting this season, 7-2 in Carolina. The Canucks are winless in six (0-5-1). The Canes are on a tear, six straight wins.
At home, Manny Malhotra likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Hurricanes’ first line. Don’t read much into Lankinen’s record against the Hurricanes.

items.text: Andrei Svechnikov has a point in five straight games against Vancouver, with a goal in each of the last four, and 9 points in his last five against them.
The Hurricanes are newly without Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal, and have had to make do without Seth Jarvis and Alexander Nikishin all season.
The Canucks are newly without Marco Rossi, and have had to make do without Thatcher Demko all season. Kevin Lankinen is expected to start.
Mark Jankowski has scored in five straight games.
